messages:
Olivia Park: Quick sketch — proposal to push short-lived 'stream windows' (per-connection, soft memory/bandwidth budgets) into the edge proxy and keep only canonical session metadata + retry history in the control plane. Edge owns buffering, prefetch, and early-abort to bound memory per connection.

Kevin Zhao: Do you mean we split responsibility by lifetime? edge = ephemeral window state, control plane = durable session/ticket info?

Olivia Park: Exactly. Edge state: window_id, seq_high, bytes_used, outstanding_prefetch. Control plane: session_id, model_variant, retry_policy, billing_consumer_id, canonical offset for long-lived resume.

Javier Mendez: Main motivation? Is it latency (avoid roundtrip to control plane for small handoffs) or safety (limit per-conn mem)?

Olivia Park: Both. Latency for steady streaming clients and memory safety when many idle-but-warm clients exist. Also simplifies edge autoscaling — edge can evict windows locally under OOM pressure without touching control-plane session store.

Samir Patel: How do we handle midstream failover? if a client reconnects to a different edge we need to reconstruct window state or fall back to control-plane resume. That sounds like possible duplication of in-flight tokens/billing risk.

Olivia Park: Two modes. Fast path: same-edge reconnects -> edge reconstructs from local checkpoint headers (no control-plane hop). Slow path: different-edge -> client provides session_id + last_ack_offset, control-plane issues a resume token and the new edge pulls canonical state. We keep resume conservative: only allow resume up to last acknowledged token to avoid double-charging.

Rita Chen: Can you show the header format clients/SDKs would use?

Olivia Park: Sure — rough header prototype:

```
X-Stream-Window: id=wnd-12345; seq=42; ack=40; budget_bytes=65536; ttl=10s
X-Resume-Session: sid=svc-9f2a; last_ack=40; resume_sig=sha256(...)
```

Edge uses X-Stream-Window to apply local admission and prefetch. If resume header present but window missing, edge initiates slow-path resume with control plane.

Kevin Zhao: What about booking/billing semantics? If edge prefetches tokens and then crashes, who gets charged? We can't have silent token loss.

Javier Mendez: We should decouple token accounting from physical prefetch. Edge can speculatively prefetch but must checkpoint prefetch requests into control-plane append-only log or at least mark them as transient so billing is gated on ack from model runtime. Otherwise accounting mismatch will be a disaster.

Olivia Park: Agreed — design constraint: speculative prefetch allowed but chargeable units only committed by the model backend. Edge keeps a local provisional count and reconciliation window with the control plane (piggyback on resume or a periodic flush). If edge disappears before reconciliation, provisional counts are discarded and model backend decides. We'll introduce a "provisional" tag in billing events.

Samir Patel: Reconciliation frequency affects cost/latency. If we flush too often, we lose latency benefits; too rarely and we risk bigger reconciliation deltas. Suggestion: adaptive flush: small flows flush on disconnect/resume; large/premium tenants flush every N seconds.

Rita Chen: Security: resume_sig needs to be HMAC with tenant key (KMS). Control plane vends signed resume tokens to clients/edges. No unsigned resume allowed. Also tie tokens to max_resume_window to avoid long-lived replay.

ingress-bot: Created RFC draft: https://rfc.internal/edge-windowing (added Olivia's sketch + header proto).

Kevin Zhao: Edge eviction: if edge evicts a window under memory pressure, what do we tell client? instant abort or graceful fallback? I prefer graceful fallback: emit a stable error code and a recommended reconnect flow that includes last_ack offset.

Olivia Park: Proposal: eviction -> graceful partial-abort trailer with code `EDGE_WINDOW_EVICT` plus ResumeHint header containing session_id + last_ack. Client SDKs auto-reconnect to control-plane-proxied edge or try same-edge if sticky set.

Javier Mendez: Observability: we need per-window metrics: bytes_prefetched, evictions, reconcilations_delta, speculative_prefetch_ratio. Also traces for slow-path resumes to track control-plane latency impact.

Samir Patel: One more tradeoff: pushing window logic to edge increases surface area of bugs (consistency bugs). We should keep window logic small — admission, byte accounting, and TTL. Anything requiring global coordination (sticky failovers, billing reconciliation) must be in control plane.

Olivia Park: Agreed. Action items: 
- Olivia/Rita: flesh out header proto & resume token lifecycle (this week)
- Javier: metric list + dashboard template (next sprint)
- Kevin/Samir: simulate eviction/reconnect scenarios with 10k concurrent clients and report reconcilation deltas (POC by end of sprint)
- I'll update the RFC with explicit error codes and flow diagrams.

Rita Chen: One nit: ensure the SDKs expose a reconnect hook that can insert resume_sig; otherwise apps will leak complexity to end users.

Olivia Park: Good call. We'll add an SDK-level auto-resume toggle (on by default for PLG flows).

Kevin Zhao: Sounds promising. Keen to see the POC numbers before we commit to rollout. :+1:

Olivia Park: Thanks all — next touchpoint after RFC update.
